$comment: data/verification-verdicts.json — the standing yay/nay verdicts of docs/VERIFICATION.md, extracted by hand into a machine-readable datum.  WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  docs/VERIFICATION.md is the record of every judging wave, and it is prose: a superseding header, then one markdown table per wave, each wave overriding rows in the last.  The frames and the judge's own verdict.json files live OUTSIDE this repository (VERIFICATION.md:31-34, 'local dev-artifacts/foil-verify/'), so there is nothing machine-readable to read.  The contribution queue needs the STANDING set — what is still a nay today, after every wave — and a build step that parsed six markdown tables and replayed their supersessions would be a prose parser pretending to be a data source.  So the extraction happens ONCE, by hand, here, with the doc line numbers that justify every row; the builder reads this file and never opens the doc.  HOW TO UPDATE.  When a wave lands in VERIFICATION.md, edit this file in the SAME commit: flip the verdict, bump `wave`/`judgedOn`, move the old state into `supersedes`, and update `docLines`.  tools/task-queue/build.ts fails the build if a patternId here is not an implemented pattern id, so a rename cannot silently orphan a verdict.  WHAT A NAY IS.  VERIFICATION.md:36-43: each render is a deterministic 8-frame tilt sweep judged on four 0-5 dimensions (static appearance / tilt motion / layer character / color travel); match=true requires every dimension >= 3.  A nay is match=false.  THE CAVEAT THIS FILE CARRIES.  Several nays are motion claims that a still-frame judge structurally cannot score.  VERIFICATION.md:759-764: 'Still-frame motion blindness now has FIVE data points ... Chey's live tilt remains the arbiter for motion claims.'  Those rows carry stillFrameBlind: true and ask: 'live-tilt' — the contribution they need is a HUMAN VERDICT ON A TILTING CARD, not another GLSL round.  Answering them with more shader work is the documented wrong move.
